Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training
Demonstrated experience personally soliciting gifts of $10,000 or more from individuals.
One or more years of experience in a frontline, face-to-face fundraising role involving leadership-level gifts of $10,000 or greater.

The Assistant Director of Donor Relations serves as a frontline fundraising professional responsible for identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding leadership-level prospects within the Division of Social Sciences. This position independently manages a fundraising portfolio of approximately $500,000 - $1,000,000 and works with Prospect Research, development colleagues, and current donors to identify and develop new prospects through the Division's pipeline program, the Dean's Circle, and leadership-giving opportunities. The Assistant Director of Donor Relations focuses on increasing annual and special gift support, with particular emphasis on unrestricted giving.
Leadership Giving & Portfolio Management
Independently manages a dynamic fundraising portfolio of approximately $500,000 - $1,000,000, consisting of 120-200 leadership giving prospects.
Conducts approximately 120 substantive donor contacts annually through in-person meetings, Zoom, and telephone engagement.
Identifies, qualifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards prospects and donors to increase annual and special gift support.

Partners with the Director of Annual Programs and Assistant Dean of Development to expand membership in the Deans Circle and 1903 Society and supports key fundraising initiatives, including Big Give, through solicitation of challenge gifts and donor participation.

Collaborates with Major Gift Officers, Annual Giving Officers, Gift Administration, Stewardship, Institutes/Centers, University Relations, and campus development colleagues to ensure prospects are appropriately engaged, solicited, and stewarded.
Directly or indirectly secures $500,000 - $1,000,000 in unrestricted support annually and increases giving among personally and jointly managed prospects by 10-30%.
Annual & Long-Term Fundraising Strategy
Supports annual and long-term strategies to increase the number of donors at leadership giving levels.
Uses knowledge of the donor and prospect base to inform outreach, appeals, and department-specific fundraising messaging.
Participates in short- and long-range strategic planning to achieve fundraising goals and align philanthropic opportunities with donor interests.
Donor Stewardship & Communications
Coordinates donor stewardship efforts, including donor meetings, ongoing engagement, and written and verbal communications.
Develops and contributes to persuasive fundraising and stewardship materials communicating the strengths and priorities of Leadership Giving programs, including the Deans Circle and 1903 Society.
Engages donors as appropriate for profiles and other communications and tracks donor interactions with faculty and students to inform stewardship activities.
Independently analyzes donor giving reports to identify trends, opportunities, and potential areas of donor attrition.
Uses donor data and engagement information to strengthen the leadership giving pipeline, identify prospects for increased giving, and inform cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies.
Donor Cultivation, Stewardship & Fundraising Events
Organizes, manages, and leads donor cultivation, stewardship, and fundraising events in support of divisional fundraising objectives.

Coordinates donor outreach and follow-up and works with divisional colleagues and other campus partners to use events as opportunities to cultivate prospects, strengthen donor relationships, and advance fundraising engagement.
Thorough working knowledge and understanding of fundraising, donor relations, and development concepts, principles, techniques, procedures, and practices.
Working knowledge of the campus, its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements, and infrastructure, or comparable institutional knowledge.

Thorough written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills, including political acumen, to build and maintain effective working relationships throughout the organization and with donors and other external constituencies.
Strong organizational, analytical, and critical-thinking skills, including effective decision-making, problem identification and resolution, and project management.
Ability to independently develop and implement donor identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies in support of established fundraising goals.
Ability to analyze donor and prospect information to identify fundraising opportunities, strengthen the donor pipeline, and inform engagement strategies.
Ability to articulate a compelling case for annual and leadership-level philanthropic support for higher education.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and fundraising initiatives independently while working collaboratively with colleagues and campus partners.
Strong skills in maintaining confidentiality and appropriately handling sensitive donor and institutional information.
Ability and motivation to meet or exceed established fundraising goals and objectives.
Ability to occasionally travel and work evenings and weekends as required to meet with donors and support fundraising activities.
